newsitem.title: USA: Clinton asks for labor help on Herman confirmation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton asks for labor help on Herman confirmation.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Sunday appealed to union activists to put pressure on the Senate to confirm his designated labor secretary, Alexis Herman.

Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said Monday that the Senate would not consider Herman's nomination until Clinton clarified his policy on requiring that federal construction contracts be performed by union labor.
Lott said senators were concerned that the president might be trying to carry out by executive order regulations that should be subject to a congressional vote.

"I want you to help me get Alexis Herman confirmed as Secretary of Labor," Clinton told a meeting of some 1,500 members of the United Auto Workers, in Washington for their annual legislative conference.

"She was voted out of committee unanimously and then all of a sudden they decided maybe they could get me to change some of the executive actions I have taken to try to prevent anti-union activities when it comes to government contracts," Clinton told the union members.
"Now, I don't think that's a very good way to run a railroad," he said.
A union official said that union members would be canvassing Capitol Hill this week on a number of labor-related issues, including Herman's nomination.
AFL-CIO president John Sweeney last week criticized Lott's decision on Herman's nomination as "last-minute hostage-taking".
